patient_overview.name: Annamae Hauck
patient_overview.description: Annamae Hauck is a 46-year-old single woman from Bridgewater, New Jersey, who works full-time and lives in a crowded household of seven. She comes in for nutrition counseling tied to her hypertension and severe obesity management, but she is blunt about not seeing much point in the visit. She rattles off her blood pressure readings and lab numbers from memory, impatient with anything that feels like a lecture, and makes clear she's been managing her chronic back, neck, and sinus issues for over a decade without much change. She comes across as sharp, matter-of-fact, and mildly defensive about her weight and drinking.

demographics.occupation: Billing coordinator at a regional orthopedic practice
demographics.cultural_context: Annamae grew up in central New Jersey in a large, loud family where meals were whatever was fastest to get on the table between someone's shift and someone's practice. She values efficiency and directness, and she sees cooking as a chore with no payoff when you're single and feeding only yourself most nights, even though her current household is packed with relatives. She doesn't tie her eating habits to any particular heritage or tradition — it's just what's practical.

medical_history: Body mass index 40+ - severely obese since 2001
current_symptoms: Ongoing low back pain described as a constant dull ache, worse by end of a work shift
Neck stiffness, especially after sitting at a desk for long stretches
Occasional burning with urination that she says 'comes and goes, I know the drill by now'
Sinus pressure and congestion flare-ups a few times a year
General fatigue she attributes to 'just getting older'
clinical_findings: Severely obese body habitus consistent with BMI 45.3
Mild tenderness to palpation of lumbar paraspinal muscles and reduced cervical range of motion
Gait slightly slowed, favoring lower back when rising from chair

medications.name: {28 (norethindrone 0.35 MG Oral Tablet) } Pack [Jolivette 28 Day]
medications.adherence: Takes it consistently, says it's 'the one pill I never forget because I don't want more kids'
medications.patient_concerns: No real complaints; views it as routine and unrelated to her weight or blood pressure

medications.name: Hydrochlorothiazide 25 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Mostly consistent but admits to skipping it 'maybe once a week when I forget my pillbox at my sister's house'
medications.patient_concerns: Says it makes her urinate more at work which is inconvenient during her shift

medications.name: lisinopril 10 MG Oral Tablet
medications.adherence: Consistent, takes it with the hydrochlorothiazide each morning
medications.patient_concerns: Mentions a dry cough sometimes but says 'it's not bad enough to call the doctor about'

medications.name: Vitamin B12 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution
medications.frequency: Monthly injection at her doctor's office
medications.adherence: Keeps the appointment every month, calls it 'the one thing I don't let slide'
medications.patient_concerns: None stated; she likes that it's quick and doesn't require her to remember a daily pill

supplements_and_otc: Ibuprofen 200mg tablets, taken most days for back and neck pain
Occasional antacid tablets after large or late meals

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Heavy reliance on frozen dinners, deli sandwiches, and takeout; minimal home cooking
food_preferences: Rotisserie chicken from the supermarket deli
Diet soda, several cans a day
Italian takeout subs from a shop near her office
Pretzels and chips as evening snacks
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Portion sizes at dinner, often eaten standing at the counter after a long shift
Frequency and amount of wine consumed on weeknights versus what she first reports
Salt content of frequent takeout and frozen meals relative to her hypertension
Lack of vegetables beyond what comes pre-packaged in a meal kit
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Skips or rushes breakfast, grabs a sandwich at her desk for lunch, eats a large convenience dinner late in the evening after work
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly diet soda and coffee; says she 'doesn't really do water'
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Mostly sedentary desk job; parks far from the building entrance 'to get a little walking in' but no structured exercise
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Ex-smoker, quit roughly 8 years ago; drinks wine most evenings though she initially describes it as 'just a glass here and there'
nutrition_profile.sleep: Reports 6 to 7 hours, often interrupted by noise from the full household

psychosocial_profile.personality: Blunt, impatient, no-nonsense; wants the bottom line without a lot of preamble
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Precise and factual, cites her own numbers and dates readily, gets irritated by vague or 'preachy' explanations
goals: Get her blood pressure readings to stop coming up at every visit
Manage her back and neck pain well enough to keep working full shifts
Avoid another round of antibiotics for a UTI
concerns: Being told to overhaul her whole diet when she feels she doesn't have time to cook
Her weight being blamed for everything from her back pain to her blood pressure
Being lectured by someone younger than her kids
beliefs: She believes her weight is mostly genetic since 'half my family is built this way'
She believes cooking for one person is a waste of time and money
She doesn't think a glass or two of wine a night matters much
motivations: Staying employed and functional given her physical job demands
Not wanting to depend on her family for help with daily tasks
fears: Losing mobility to the point she can't work
barriers: Crowded, chaotic household makes meal planning hard
Long work hours leave little energy for cooking
Family does not take her health conditions seriously and jokes about her diet
strengths: Organized about her medical appointments and medication schedule
Articulate and able to track her own numbers accurately
Still physically capable of working full-time despite pain
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Lives with extended family (household of 7) who she describes as 'loud and unhelpful' about her health, often pushing food on her or dismissing her concerns
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Precontemplation; does not see a strong reason to change her eating or drinking habits right now

initial_information: States her blood pressure was 97/64 at her last visit and she thinks that's 'basically fine'
Mentions she's been dealing with back and neck pain since 2014 and 'it's just part of life now'
Says she eats mostly frozen dinners and takeout because cooking for herself isn't worth the effort
discoverable_information: Admits she skips breakfast most days and eats a big dinner late at night
Reveals she drinks diet soda multiple times a day instead of water
Mentions her family at home teases her about her weight and doesn't take her hypertension seriously
Describes her job as a billing coordinator with long hours sitting at a desk
reluctant_information: When asked directly about alcohol, eventually says she has 'maybe two glasses of wine' most weeknights, not just 'here and there' as she first said
Admits she sometimes has a third glass on weekends when family gatherings get going
hidden_information: Annamae has actually been drinking close to a bottle of wine on weekend nights for the past year, which she has not disclosed to any provider
She has quietly stopped filling her hydrochlorothiazide refill on time twice this year because she didn't want to deal with the bathroom breaks during a busy work week

possible_patient_reactions: 'It's just a glass or two, nothing crazy.'
'Why does this matter if my pressure was fine last visit?'
Becomes more forthcoming once she feels she isn't being judged

opportunities.learning_objective: Assess readiness to change and apply motivational interviewing in a precontemplation stage patient
